texts.preamble: Shibasis Tripathy vs State Of Odisha And Others .... Opposite ... on 19 November, 2025 Author: R.K. Pattanaik Bench: R.K. Pattanaik In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack W.P. (C) No.21530 of 2025 Shibasis Tripathy .... Petitioner Mr. A.P. Bose, Advocate -Versus- State of Odisha and others .... Opposite Parties Mr. P.K. Sahoo, Asc Mr. A.Mohanta, Advocate for O.P.No.4 Coram: Mr. Justice R.K. Pattanaik
texts.facts: 2. Instant writ petition is filed by the petitioner to direct opposite party Nos. 2 to 4 to renew the agreement i.e. Annexure-1 and not to disturb his physical possession as there is no default in payment of license fees nor any violation of the terms and conditions thereof.
texts.arguments: 3. Mr. Bose, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a license holder to run a hotel and is having trade license and food safety license issued to him and refers to Annexure-2 series. It is also submitted that the petitioner had made the deposits as required in terms of the license, hence, therefore, opposite party No.4 should be directed to renew the same without taking any coercive action. Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel for opposite party No.4 refers to the counter affidavit and submits that the petitioner is a defaulter and there can be no renewal of license in his favour. As per the affidavit, according to Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel, the petitioner was to make payment of license fee of Rs.2,000/- and deposited an amount of Rs. 50,000/- on 9th February, 2021 as against the outstanding dues of Rs. 1,26,000/- and it has become Rs.1,72,000/- payable till July, 2025 and therefore, no case is made out for renewal, hence, the writ petition should be dismissed. 4.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Mr. Bose, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a license holder to run a hotel and is having trade license and food safety license issued to him and refers to Annexure-2 series. It is also submitted that the petitioner had made the deposits as required in terms of the license, hence, therefore, opposite party No.4 should be directed to renew the same without taking any coercive action. Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel for opposite party No.4 refers to the counter affidavit and submits that the petitioner is a defaulter and there can be no renewal of license in his favour.
texts.respondent_arguments: As per the affidavit, according to Mr. Mohanta, learned counsel, the petitioner was to make payment of license fee of Rs.2,000/- and deposited an amount of Rs. 50,000/- on 9th February, 2021 as against the outstanding dues of Rs. 1,26,000/- and it has become Rs.1,72,000/- payable till July, 2025 and therefore, no case is made out for renewal, hence, the writ petition should be dismissed. 4.
